title: What is known about 1RB0LA_0LC0RD_0RE1LA_0RC1LB_1LE0LF_1RD---
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0LA_0LC0RD_0RE1LA_0RC1LB_1LE0LF_1RD---.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. At the left end the tape is a list of blocks (10)^x separated by single 0s, alternating big and small; in long stretches every pair (x, y) becomes (x − δ, y + δ) with the same δ between two left visits. The collisions when a block runs out are not understood. Halting needs F on a 1, entered only from E on a 1: never one step away in the first 3·106 steps.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 32,393 cells have been visited and 16,156 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: power/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.512). Right of the start it grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.238).

claims.title: Shift rules of the sweeps
claims.text: Lean proves, for every count and every tape around, the shift rules of the sweeps: C crosses (10)^n rightward, A crosses (10)^n and (01)^n leftward (the second turning into (10)^n), C crosses (01)^n leftward; 4 steps per copy each.

claims.title: The tape is a list of pairs of blocks
claims.text: Whenever the visited part grows on the left (in A), the tape reads A>0 0^3 (10)^x1 0 (10)^y1 0 (10)^x2 0 (10)^y2 0 … with x big and y small, e.g. at step 140,133,553: 442 61 407 61 407 64 381 62 340 56 303 52 …, and a short irregular end near the right edge.

claims.title: The drift: (x, y) → (x − δ, y + δ)
claims.text: Between two left extensions every pair loses δ from its big block and gives it to its small one, the same δ for the whole stretch: step 140,133,553 → 140,405,051 has δ = 6 for all of 442 61 407 61 407 64 381 62 340 → 436 67 401 67 401 70 375 68 334. So x + y is kept and the separator inside each pair moves left by δ while the separators between pairs stay. δ varies from visit to visit (2, 4, 6, …); in some visits the list is re-indexed from the left end, and when a block runs out the pair is rebuilt.
claims.where: the left-extension samples, 226 transitions to 3·10<sup>9</sup> steps

claims.title: Never one step from a halt
claims.text: The machine halts when F reads a 1, and F is entered only from E reading a 1 (E1 → 0LF). In the first 3·10<sup>6</sup> steps E reads a 1 122,248 times, always with a 0 to its left.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. The drift is measured, not proved, and the collisions (a small block reaching 0, a new pair at the left end) are not written as rules. This looks like a particle system whose collisions decide everything; it may be chaotic.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. This machine's tape is a list of pairs of blocks, and the boundaries inside the pairs drift through the list like particles. This page shows the list, the drift, and what is proved.

facts.text: No halt in the C simulator; 32,393 cells visited.
No halt, proved in Lean; the first 10,000 by the kernel alone.
The growth shape of the two sides of the tape (see below).

sections.heading: A list of pairs of blocks
html: Write a for 10. Each time the tape grows at the left end, it reads (step 140,133,553)
a list of blocks of 10 separated by single 0s, big and small in turn: pairs (442, 61), (407, 61), (407, 64), (381, 62), …

sections.heading: The separators drift
html: Every pair moved 6 from its big block to its small block: (x, y) → (x − δ, y + δ), the same δ everywhere. The 0 in the middle of each pair walked left by 6 blocks; the 0s between pairs did not move. δ is different at different visits, and when a block runs out the pair is rebuilt; those collisions are not yet understood. Measured, not proved.

sections.heading: What a halt would need
html: The machine stops only in F reading a 1, and F is entered only from E reading a 1 (moving left). So a halt needs E on a 1 with a 1 to its left. In the first 3·106 steps E reads a 1 122,248 times and the cell to its left is always 0. Whether a collision of separators can ever produce that is open.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.512). Right of the start it grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.238).
After 109 steps the tape spans 32,393 cells (23,630 left of the start, 531 right), with a density of 1s of 0.499.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

family: list of block pairs with drifting separators
summary: The tape is a list of pairs of (10)-blocks (big, small); between left-end visits every pair moves the same amount from its big block to its small one, so one kind of separator drifts while the other stays, and their collisions reshape the list.
